content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Before starting treatment with ospemifene, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Use this medication regularly to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects may include hot flashes, vaginal discharge, muscle spasms, and sweating. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious complications related to blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Your risk of blood clots may increase if you are severely dehydrated, have a history of blood clots, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, stroke, or if you are immobile for extended periods (e.g., during long flights or bed rest). Inform your doctor if you have any of these conditions before using this medication. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking ospemifene, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery or will be confined to a bed or chair for an extended period, as these conditions may increase your risk of blood clots. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of ospemifene from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. You should undergo a complete physical examination, including breast and pelvic exams, and a PAP test (to screen for vaginal cancer) as directed by your doctor, typically at least once a year. Periodic mammograms should also be performed as recommended by your doctor. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any unusual vaginal bleeding, breast pain, or lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal methods. This information was last revised in July 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most up-to-date and complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
